review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Database data versus DBMS software; SQLite and deductive software; table structures and definitions; integrity constraints; transaction execution, records, commit and rollback; selected rename-generated language tags.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. SQLite, PostgreSQL and the CORAL project support technical extensions. Source prose and code are not copied. Qualified labels, intersections and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U3 with unspecified strength. Preserve home contexts and previously valid genera. The old СУБД term and parent of the deductive system determine the selected software readings. SQL constraint kinds and arity restrictions are separate axes.

sense_decisions.scope: The record already inherits the Russian СУБД concept. CORAL provides a primary-source example of implemented deductive database software. The data collection of facts and rules is not equated with that software.
DBMS software for relational data; not the relational database itself.
DBMS software running within its host application process, without requiring a separate database-server process.
The intersection of in-process embedding and relational data management.
A relational DBMS with a distinct database-server program serving client requests.

sense_decisions.alignment: operation associated with the DBMS meaning
sense_decisions.scope: An operation that creates, maintains or accesses a database through database-management software.
A record occurring in a database table; duplicates and unspecified row order are possible.
A named column in a database table, not an architectural pillar or a newspaper article.
A description of database structures, distinct from the stored rows and from a SQL namespace named schema.
A description of a table structure, distinct from the table data and the whole database schema.
The database-schema specialization of the existing broader schema-matching process.
An auxiliary data structure supporting access to database rows; not an array position or a guaranteed speedup.
A specified rule restricting admissible database values or relationships; distinguish the rule from the data.
A SQL constraint expressed by a checking predicate; do not identify UNKNOWN with FALSE.
The SQL constraint excluding NULL for the constrained column.
The declared SQL uniqueness constraint; NULL treatment is not assumed identical across implementations.
The SQL constraint designating primary-key columns; do not impose a universal storage or index implementation.
A constraint scoped to one constrained column of the local table, irrespective of column/table syntax.
A constraint involving multiple constrained columns of the local table; not every table-level declaration has this arity.
A foreign-key constraint with one local constrained column.
A foreign-key constraint over multiple local columns.
The referenced table is the same table; no requirement to reference another table is inherited.
A primary-key constraint spanning multiple columns.
A structured record describing a database transaction; not the transaction execution itself.
The operation of committing a database transaction; not a source-control commit object.
Discarding uncommitted transactional changes, either for a whole transaction or back to a savepoint.
A designated point within a transaction supporting partial rollback; not a backup file or a committed database snapshot.
Rollback restricted to changes after an existing savepoint; earlier changes remain within the transaction.
NoSQL remains a broad data-model label; no unsupported claim that all NoSQL systems reject SQL is added.
Reuse the existing tabular data structure; its code-page child is outside this batch.
Reuse the existing structured record sense rather than importing sporting or music-record homonyms.
Preserve the broader schema-matching process and add a database-specific target restriction.
Only the database-as-component assertion is rejected; broader SQL language and query semantics remain queued.
Keep its existing СУБД genus while making the software sense explicit; do not treat stored facts/rules as executable software.
The dictionary transaction synset concerns group/commercial activity, not the technical database execution.
An index structure is not the already existing integer array index 24485.

review.limits: No database deployment, application test suite, schema migration or user-data transaction is executed. No universal index speedup, unique row order, mandatory primary key, foreign-key NOT NULL rule, primary-key-only reference rule or implementation-independent NULL policy is asserted. SQLite can be used inside a server application without becoming a separate server process. General data schemas, SQL schema namespaces, view/materialized-view distinctions, relational algebra, SQL lifecycle and foreign-key column sets remain queued.

exclusion_review.decision: Preserve the clear shared-descendant scans and all upper exclusions and explicit negations.

review.collision_decision: No new-term normalized collision accepted. Reuse existing СУБД, SQLite, table, record, foreign-key and transaction records with explicit senses.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.

repairs.reason: A DBMS is software; an organized database is the managed data. OEWN 2025: oewn-06601066-n.
SQLite is an embedded relational database engine, not a database data collection. Source: https://www.sqlite.org/about.html
The database data collection was assigned an active storage capability. Retain its data/content relation and represent the managing software separately.
Use the existing tabular data-structure genus rather than the containing database. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-basics.html
A foreign-key constraint is a database integrity rule, not a kind of database. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/ddl-constraints.html
A SQL language is not composed of a relational database. Preserve the separate existing language-use relation; do not confuse a language and the data managed with it.
A database transaction in the execution sense is a computing operation, not the information object recording it. Source: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/tutorial-transactions.html
